rationale: A model removed stops shooting back; a model on 1 wound does not. AUDIT 0.10's class of defect is spreading damage across two targets and killing neither. Here an enemy Blade Champion is left on 1 of 6 wounds next to a fresh Custodian Guard squad, both in range of the firing Custodian Guard's guardian spears. Finishing the wounded character is worth more than chipping the fresh squad, and the marginal-value allocator is supposed to know that. The exam checks the AI ALLOCATED at least one weapon to the wounded unit — not that the dice killed it, which would be a coin flip in an exam's clothes.

assert.name: a weapon was aimed at the wounded character

why_it_fails_today: The marginal-value allocator prices damage against a target's REMAINING wounds but has no notion of what the target will do on the reply, so a 1-wound character and a fresh squad compete on damage efficiency alone. D3's one-ply opponent reply is what makes 'it dies before it acts again' worth something.
measured_2026_08_07: FAIL — this is the expected result until D3 lands.
